s1.syndrome_frame: Painless swelling of the hard palate with slow and symmetrical growth
salient_findings: Painless swelling in the molar region of the hard palate
Swelling grew slowly and symmetrically over 10-12 weeks
Firm, elastic, non-ulcerated swelling on both sides of the hard palate
key_facts: 41-year-old man with no significant medical history
10-12 week history of painless swelling in the molar region of the hard palate
Swelling grew slowly and symmetrically
Denied dysphagia, odynophagia, or systemic symptoms
Family history was unremarkable
1.5 x 3.0 cm firm, elastic, non-ulcerated swelling on both sides of the hard palate
No cervical lymphadenopathy detected
Routine serum chemistry was within normal limits
Serologies for hepatitis A, B, and C were negative
Palatal bone appeared uninvolved during excision
Wound healed slowly over 4-5 weeks

shortlist.label: Torus Palatinus
shortlist.why_kept: Painless, slow-growing, and symmetrical swelling on the hard palate

shortlist.label: Palatal Fibromatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Firm, elastic, non-ulcerated swelling on the hard palate

shortlist.label: Giant Cell Granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of a painless swelling on the hard palate

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic Adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common salivary gland tumor that can present as a painless swelling

shortlist.label: Fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor that can cause a slow-growing, painless swelling on the hard palate

raw.rationale: The slow and symmetrical growth of the swelling, its location on the hard palate, and the absence of ulceration or lymphadenopathy are consistent with Torus Palatinus, a benign bony growth that typically occurs in the midline of the hard palate but can also occur bilaterally.

rejected.label: Palatal Fibromatosis
rejected.why: While it could explain the slow growth, it is less common and typically involves the soft tissues more aggressively.

rejected.label: Giant Cell Granuloma
rejected.why: Usually presents with more rapid growth and can be painful, which contradicts the painless nature of the swelling in this case.

rejected.label: Pleomorphic Adenoma
rejected.why: Most common salivary gland tumor, but it typically presents as a solitary, mobile, and painless mass, often in the parotid gland or submandibular gland, not bilaterally on the hard palate.

rejected.label: Fibroma
rejected.why: Could be a consideration due to the firm and elastic nature of the swelling, but the bilateral and symmetrical presentation is more suggestive of Torus Palatinus.
